test_cases.description: Clean vector geometry with shape, fill, viewBox, and automatic xmlns injection
test_cases.raw_input: <svg viewBox="0 0 100 100"><rect x="10" y="10" width="80" height="80" fill="blue"/></svg>
test_cases.sanitized_output: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100"><rect x="10" y="10" width="80" height="80" fill="blue"/></svg>
test_cases.security_notes: Preserves standard SVG primitives while guaranteeing strict SVG namespace on root element.

test_cases.description: Hostile embedded executable <script> tags attempting inline DOM XSS
test_cases.raw_input: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 200 200"><script>window.__xss = 1; alert(document.domain);</script><circle cx="100" cy="100" r="50" fill="green"/></svg>
test_cases.sanitized_output: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 200 200"><circle cx="100" cy="100" r="50" fill="green"/></svg>
test_cases.security_notes: DOMPurify SVG profile strips <script> elements and inline text execution payloads completely.

test_cases.description: Hostile <foreignObject> embedding arbitrary HTML, iframes, and cross-origin widgets
test_cases.raw_input: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 200 200"><foreignObject width="100" height="100"><body xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml"><iframe src="https://evil.test"></iframe></body></foreignObject><rect width="50" height="50"/></svg>
test_cases.security_notes: FORBID_TAGS strips <foreignObject>, <body>, and <iframe>, eliminating HTML context breakout.

test_cases.description: Hostile <image> elements with remote HTTP/HTTPS URLs attempting user IP and cookie tracking
test_cases.raw_input: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><image href="https://evil.test/track.png" xlink:href="https://evil.test/track2.png" width="50" height="50" /><circle r="10"/></svg>
test_cases.security_notes: FORBID_TAGS strips <image> elements completely. Second-layer attribute sanitizer blocks external network fetches.

test_cases.description: Hostile <style> elements with @import directives attempting CSS exfiltration and layout hijacking
test_cases.raw_input: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><style>@import url("https://evil.test/evil.css"); body { background: red; }</style><rect width="20" height="20"/></svg>
test_cases.security_notes: FORBID_TAGS strips <style> tags and FORBID_ATTR strips style attributes, enforcing style-src self CSP.

test_cases.description: Hostile SMIL <animate> elements mutating xlink:href to javascript: URI execution vectors
test_cases.raw_input: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><animate attributeName="href" to="javascript:alert(1)" /><animateTransform attributeName="transform" type="rotate" /><rect width="20" height="20"/></svg>
test_cases.security_notes: FORBID_TAGS strips animate, animateTransform, animateMotion, and set elements.

test_cases.description: Hostile inline event handlers (onload, onclick, onerror, onmouseover) on valid SVG geometry
test_cases.raw_input: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><circle cx="50" cy="50" r="40" onload="alert(1)" onclick="stealCookies()" onmouseover="track()"/></svg>
test_cases.security_notes: Dual-layer DOMPurify event handler stripping and post-parse attribute scrubber remove all on* attributes.

test_cases.description: Hostile <use> tags referencing off-origin remote SVG resource files
test_cases.security_notes: Href regex /^[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+$/ strictly strips non-local href attributes, preventing cross-origin asset pulls.

test_cases.description: Hostile recursive <use> element referencing its own enclosing definition ID
test_cases.security_notes: Acyclic DAG depth-first search detects visited target node and rejects with SVG_USE_CYCLE before serialization.

test_cases.description: Hostile mutual recursive loop between two distinct <use> elements (A -> B -> A)
test_cases.security_notes: Detects mutual recursion in reference graph and rejects before browser renderer causes stack overflow.

test_cases.description: Valid deep <use> chain at exact maximum allowed depth of 4 (l1 -> l2 -> l3 -> l4)
test_cases.raw_input: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><defs><rect id="l4" width="10" height="10"/><g id="l3"><use href="#l4"/></g><g id="l2"><use href="#l3"/></g><g id="l1"><use href="#l2"/></g></defs><use href="#l1"/></svg>
test_cases.sanitized_output: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><defs><rect id="l4" width="10" height="10"/><g id="l3"><use href="#l4"/></g><g id="l2"><use href="#l3"/></g><g id="l1"><use href="#l2"/></g></defs><use href="#l1"/></svg>

test_cases.description: Hostile deep <use> chain exceeding maximum allowed depth of 4 (step1 -> step2 -> step3 -> step4 -> step5)
test_cases.raw_input: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><defs><rect id="step5" width="10" height="10"/><g id="step4"><use href="#step5"/></g><g id="step3"><use href="#step4"/></g><g id="step2"><use href="#step3"/></g><g id="step1"><use href="#step2"/></g></defs><use href="#step1"/></svg>
test_cases.security_notes: Exceeds MAX_SVG_USE_DEPTH (4) and is rejected with SVG_USE_MAX_DEPTH.

test_cases.description: Exponential <use> expansion resulting in exactly 500 expanded DOM nodes
test_cases.raw_input: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><defs><g id="baseGroup"><!-- 49 rects + 1 group = 50 nodes --></g></defs><!-- 10 uses of baseGroup = 500 expanded nodes --></svg>
test_cases.security_notes: Passes because expanded node count is <= MAX_SVG_EXPANDED_NODES (500).

test_cases.description: Hostile exponential <use> billion-laughs bomb resulting in 550 expanded DOM nodes (> 500 limit)
test_cases.raw_input: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><defs><g id="baseGroup"><!-- 49 rects + 1 group = 50 nodes --></g></defs><!-- 11 uses of baseGroup = 550 expanded nodes --></svg>
test_cases.security_notes: Rejected with SVG_EXPANSION_LIMIT_EXCEEDED before client browser freezes from DOM explosion.

test_cases.description: Oversized SVG payload exceeding client 2 MiB boundary (2,097,153 bytes)
test_cases.security_notes: TextEncoder byte length check rejects oversized payloads immediately before parsing.

test_cases.description: Malformed SVG XML syntax causing DOMParser parsererror
test_cases.security_notes: DOMParser parsererror detected and rejected with SVG_PARSE_ERROR.
Whitespace check rejects empty input with SVG_EMPTY.
